ITEM 4. INFORMATION ON THE COMPANY
A. History and Development of the Company
The Company was incorporated
under the laws of the Cayman Islands on August 6th, 2021, solely for the purpose of effectuating the Business Combination, which was consummated
on May 17, 2023. The Company has no material assets other than its interests in ASGL and GBRG acquired in the Business Combination and
does not operate any business other than through ASGL, its wholly-owned subsidiary. ASGL is a Cayman Islands exempted company. See Item
5-Operating and Financial Review and Prospects for a discussion of ASGL’s operating and financial review and prospects for the
year ended December 31, 2025.
The mailing address of the
Company’s principal executive office is Suite 209, No. 656 Lingshi Road, Jing’an District, Shanghai, 200072, People’s
Republic of China, and its telephone number is (86) 138-1779-6110. The Company’s official website is https://suncartech.com/. The
information contained on, or accessible through, the Company’s website is not incorporated by reference into this Report, and you
should not consider it a part of this Report.
The Company is subject to
certain of the informational filing requirements of the Exchange Act. Since the Company is a “foreign private issuer,” the
officers, directors and principal shareholders of the Company are exempt from the reporting and “short-swing” profit recovery
provisions contained in Section 16 of the Exchange Act with respect to their purchase and sale of Class A Ordinary Shares. In addition,
the Company is not required to file reports and financial statements with the SEC as frequently or as promptly as U.S. public companies
whose securities are registered under the Exchange Act. However, the Company is required to file with the SEC an Annual Report on Form
20-F containing financial statements audited by an independent accounting firm. On March 30, 2023, the Company and GBRG furnished to its
shareholders a proxy statement/prospectus relating to the Business Combination. The SEC also maintains a website at http://www.sec.gov
that contains reports and other information that the Company files with or furnishes electronically to the SEC.
B. Business Overview
Prior to the Business Combination,
the Company did not conduct any material activities other than those incidental to its formation and the matters contemplated by the Merger
Agreement, such as the making of certain required securities law filings and the establishment of merger subsidiaries. Upon the Closing,
the Company became the direct parent of ASGL (d/b/a SunCar) and conducts its business through ASGL and ASGL’s subsidiaries.

INDUSTRY OVERVIEW OF SUNCAR
Electric Vehicles (“EVs”) in China
China’s EV market reached a historic milestone in 2025, with
EVs making up almost 50% of new car sales. According to China’s Ministry of Public Security, the total number of motor vehicles
in China reached 469 million by the end of 2025. Of these, the number of EVs totaled 43.97 million, accounting for approximately 12% of
all automobiles, up from 31.40 million at the end of 2024. In 2025, 12.93 million new EVs were sold, representing approximately 49% of
all new vehicle sales, underscoring the accelerating pace of EV growth. EV wholesale sales reached 15.33 million units, a 25% annual increase.
China’s EV manufacturers, led by BYD, SAIC, Geely, and Chery, achieved record annual sales and surpassed Japanese automakers in
total passenger vehicle sales for the first time. Additionally, 66% of EVs sold in 2025 were equipped with “hands-off” automated
driving assist systems, highlighting the rapid convergence of electrification and autonomous driving technology in China’s market.
China also produced over 70% of the world’s lithium-ion batteries, with manufacturers such as CATL and BYD playing a central role
in the global EV supply chain.
Artificial intelligence (“AI”) is increasingly being integrated
into China’s EVs and their broader ecosystem. The Chinese Government is strongly encouraging EV manufacturers to incorporate AI
across all aspects of their vehicles. With 66% of China’s EV already equipped with self-driving features, the next phase of EV development
is expected to focus on fully autonomous, AI-powered vehicles. SunCar, through its partnership with ByteDance Doubao, is enabling its
EV partners to deliver the latest AI-powered insurance and services to their drivers. These include intelligent policy pricing and matching,
predictive maintenance, and advanced service routing.
Overview of China’s Auto Insurance Market
The insurance market in China
is highly concentrated and dominated by state-owned insurance companies such as PICC, Ping An, and Pacific Insurance. The top 10 insurance
company groups collectively account for more than 90% of the market share.
Auto insurance in China consists
of two components: compulsory motor vehicle liability insurance and commercial insurance. Compulsory motor vehicle liability insurance
premiums are paid annually, with rates determined by accident records and vehicle capacity. Commercial insurance is classified into two
categories, primary and additional insurance. Commercial insurance premiums are generally determined by the vehicle’s purchase price,
traffic violation records, and other variables. These premiums are often adjusted based on the accident rate in previous years.
According to GlobalData, China’s total auto insurance market,
measured by gross written premiums, was estimated to be approximately $130 billion in 2025 and is projected to grow to approximately $166
billion by 2029. The auto insurance market is impacted by growing vehicle ownership, the expanding EV fleet (which tends to carry higher
average premiums due to specialized components and battery costs), and stricter regulatory requirements for insurance coverage. EVs accounted
for approximately 11.5% of motor insurance premiums in 2025 and are growing at more than twice the rate of the overall market, making
EV-focused insurance one of the fastest-growing segments in China’s non-life insurance industry.
The auto insurance market
in China involves two key participants: insurance companies and insurance brokers. Insurance companies are responsible for developing
and administering policies, managing them, and paying out claims, thereby assuming the associated risks of insurance policies. Insurance
agencies or brokers act as retail or wholesale intermediaries that sell and service the insurance products created by the insurance companies.
Insurance agents are not directly employed by any single insurance company. Instead, they can choose which insurance companies to represent
and which products to sell. By cooperating with various insurance companies, insurance agencies are able to offer insurance products underwritten
by different companies, giving consumers a broader range of options.
An auto eInsurance agency refers to a brokerage that leverages internet
technology to distribute auto insurance products through online sales channels, including PC portals and mobile apps. These platforms
are designed to support and drive sales to offline channels. Through the online portal, sales staff can compare quotes and policy terms
from different insurance providers. They can also recommend suitable insurance products and perform the entire insurance transaction process
for clients, including information consultation, plan design, policy selection, and payment.
44
Future Trends of the Auto eInsurance Agency
Market in China
Increasing Demand for
More Diversified Auto eInsurance Products
From the supply side, as the
market becomes more standardized and concentrated, auto eInsurance agencies are seeking to differentiate themselves, often through product
diversification. As the market gradually evolves and matures, the complexity of auto eInsurance products also keeps evolving. From the
demand side, the growing number of vehicles is bringing more customers into the market, many of whom have increasingly specific needs.
As customers become more familiar with auto eInsurance, they will demand different types of auto eInsurance policies to meet their diverse
and specific needs. In addition, the rapid growth in EV sales is expected to drive further demand in the auto eInsurance agency market,
particularly for products tailored to EV-specific risks such as battery degradation, charging infrastructure, and autonomous driving liability.
Accelerating Industry
Consolidation
With its short history relative to more developed countries, the insurance
agency market in China remains fragmented and offers significant potential for further growth and consolidation. Moreover, as the Chinese
government continues to promote the healthy and orderly development of the auto eInsurance agency market through stricter industry regulations,
barriers to entry are expected to increase and the number of market participants to decrease. As a result, auto eInsurance agencies that
are unable to afford the increasing regulatory costs, due to their lack of scale, may consider exiting the market due to intensified competition,
poor profitability, or burdensome industry regulations. In contrast, the leading players with greater scale and experience are expected
to benefit in the long run.
Technological Advancement
to Enhance Operational Efficiency
With advances in technologies, including the Internet of Things, big
data, cloud computing, large language models, and generative AI, these technologies are rapidly becoming integrated into the EV value
chain. As digitalization brings customers, vehicle manufacturers, and auto eInsurance providers closer together, auto eInsurance agencies
can initiate strategic alliances with vehicle manufacturers to better take advantage of new market opportunities and leverage improved
customer data. Ultimately, through the application of these technologies, auto eInsurance providers can develop custom auto eInsurance
products according to each individual customer’s situation. Embedded insurance platforms, integrated directly into OEM apps and
vehicle dashboards, are reshaping how insurance products are sold and renewed, with EV manufacturers increasingly acting as primary distribution
channels for their owners. Such technological trends will likely continue in the foreseeable future.
Overview of China’s Integrated Auto Service
Market
According to China’s Ministry of Public Security, by the end
of 2025 the total number of motor vehicles on China’s roads reached 469 million units, with passenger vehicles accounting for 366
million units, representing substantial annual growth from 352.68 million motor vehicles recorded in 2024. EVs totaled 43.97 million by
the end of 2025, nearly 40% more than the 31.40 million recorded at the end of 2024. This growth underscores the rapid electrification
of China’s vehicle fleet. These figures exceeded the United States and the European Union in both fleet size and growth rates.
Integrated auto service providers
refer to those companies that offer comprehensive, integrated auto services to customers through offline service channels such as 4S dealerships,
repair & maintenance stores, and other offline auto service providers.
Business-to-Business (“B2B”) integrated auto service providers
offer their products and services to business customers which primarily are comprised of banks, airlines, insurance companies, telecom
companies, online platforms such as online travel agencies, e-commerce platforms, and corporations that have such needs. Business-to-Customer
(“B2C”) integrated auto service providers offer their products and services directly to end consumers or end users. A few
online professional auto service platforms are emerging where consumers can directly purchase relevant services online.
45
Concierge auto services
mainly target enterprise customers such as banks, insurance companies, airlines, and telecom companies, among others, who tend to
centralize procurement of these services through a bidding process. The winner of the bidding supplies integrated services to these
business customers in the form of an auto service package. Banks, insurance companies, airlines, and telecom companies generally
distribute services as rewards to their VIP customers or members, and the latter can enjoy relevant services by redeeming their
reward points.
Order push mode, where a customer
requests a specific auto service, is designed to be a standardized product and is sold by an intermediate institution such as online platforms
or e-commerce companies. They tend to offer these standardized services on their platform when consumers order the services and then procure
them accordingly from integrated auto service providers.
Future Trends in the B2B Integrated Auto Service
Market in China
Increasing Demand for
Integrated Auto Service
Driven primarily by the steadily
growing number of vehicles in use, particularly EVs, there is expanding demand for various value-added services such as concierge chauffeur,
designated driving, battery maintenance, and EV charging. The benefits of these comprehensive service solutions will continue to drive
demand for integrated auto service and are expected to sustain their growth over the long run.
More Standardized Service
Delivery Procedures and Products
To better manage their extensive
service networks, a few leading players have standardized auto services and continuously improve their service delivery procedures by
enhancing the standardization of their services. Going forward, this will be a key focus for the integrated auto service providers who
aim to rapidly expand service networks without sacrificing the quality of the services delivered by their offline channel partners.
Integration and Consolidation
of the Value Chain
As profit margins are relatively
low, certain integrated auto service providers are opting to consolidate their service networks by integrating fragmented, independent
offline service providers. This allows them to expand their geographical reach and service scope cost-effectively, and promotes resource
integration in the value chain. This also results in a win-win partnership between online platforms and offline service providers. In
the future, this model is expected to be widely adopted, as industry consolidation increases with leading players acquiring or engaging
more service providers to expand the reach of their network across the country.
More Innovation in the
Online-to-Offline Business Mode
Attracted by market potential, many auto service providers have developed
their online-to-offline service platforms to deliver auto services. However, limited marketing resources, low customer loyalty, and lack
of competitive advantages are of great concern to the integrated auto service providers. Developing more innovative business models to
optimize online and offline marketing channels has become one of the priorities for current players and new entrants. This allows them
to capture opportunities in the current gas vehicle market as well as the high growth EV market, and continue to grow in an increasingly
competitive market.
46
BUSINESS OF SUNCAR
Overview
We are a leading provider of cloud, AI, and mobile app-based auto eInsurance
services, technology services, and auto services in China. For the year ended December 31, 2025, we generated revenue of $489.3 million.
Building on our leading position in these segments and the synergies between them, we offer one-stop, fully digitalized, on-demand auto
service systems to help our enterprise customers enhance the loyalty of their end customers and better serve their end customers’
needs.
Since our inception in 2007, we have amassed significant experience
in identifying and serving the expanding needs of China’s automobile owners. With the increasing prevalence of the mobile Internet
in China, we introduced online apps for our insurance and auto business in 2014 and 2015, respectively. We have built comprehensive AI-powered
digital systems for both our auto service and auto eInsurance business segments, centered on our multi-tenant, cloud-based platform which
empowers customers and service providers to optimally access and manage the types of services and insurance they desire.
For our auto eInsurance business,
we facilitate the sale of auto insurance products underwritten by major insurance companies in China. We receive commissions from these
insurance companies, which are typically a percentage of the premium paid by the policyholder. We implement, automate, and streamline
the insurance purchasing process through our proprietary AI, cloud, and mobile apps which connect our customers to the full spectrum of
products from leading insurers in China. We sell insurance policies through a network of over 64,000 external sales partners. These sales
partners include an offline auto network with frequent exposure to car owners, an online marketplace with large user traffic, and emerging
EV OEMs and service providers. As of December 31, 2025, we have branch headquarters in 31 cities across 20 provinces of China. We have
also established collaborative relationships with 35 insurance company groups (including the top 10 insurance company groups with a combined
market share of over 90%) in over 1,255 insurance company branch offices.
We operate our auto service business by offering customized auto services
to our enterprise customers, who include major banks, insurance companies, and other enterprises, all of whom have end customer demand
for auto services. These enterprise customers purchase our services for the members of their reward programs or customer loyalty programs
to use. The auto service solutions cover over 300 types of services such as car wash, oil change, tire repair, car beautification, road
assistance, flight pickup, designated driving, VIP lounge, etc. They are provided in collaboration with our auto service providers, which
are typically third-party auto service providers. As of December 31, 2025, we have established a service network of over 48,000 third-party
brick-and-mortar auto service providers, leasing companies and roadside assistance companies. With this extensive service network, we
serve over 1,520 enterprise customers.
We have built our business
as a digitalized, technology-driven provider of online platforms that enable and facilitate B2B services. We have secured 165 registered
copyrights for our computer software. Our proprietary technology solution is centered on our multi-tenant platform and cloud infrastructure.
On the auto services side, our digital platform provides API docking, front-end plug-in and module integration for our enterprise customers,
as well as efficient, user-friendly management and operations tools for our service providers. On the auto eInsurance side, our platform
empowers our insurance partners to manage all aspects of their business, including customer orders, products, commissions, and reports.
For insurance purchasers, our online insurance portal provides data-driven, AI-powered real-time quotation, pricing, underwriting, and
payments, by connecting to our market-wide insurer clients and the full spectrum of their policy selections. Our AI-powered hybrid cloud
infrastructure provides secure storage and computation to support the demands of both insurance companies and end customers.
We have started to productize
our technology into a new business line. With growing demand to efficiently manage their businesses, our auto service providers are now
paying SunCar for online tools to streamline their business workflows, manage their customer relationships, and automate order processing.
With the iterative upgrades of our technology, we are working on developing more SaaS model product offerings and plan to gradually turn
our auto service providers into our technology service customers.
We believe the synergies between
our auto service and auto eInsurance business lines enable positive feedback loops and symbiotic growth between the two business segments.
As we grow our nationwide auto service provider network, these service providers become sales partners in our auto eInsurance business.
In terms of insurance companies, when we engage with them to sell their insurance products, we also have the opportunity to engage them
as clients of our auto service solutions. We believe these business development synergies will boost our sales channels as well as client
networks in both of our business segments.
As our business is closely
connected to the automotive industry, we have embraced the recent trends of electric and smart vehicles. We are now working with leading
EV and smart car OEMs, including Tesla, Xiaomi, NIO, Li Auto, ZEEKR, SAIC, Leapmotor, XPeng, Avatr, Lotus, Seres Auto, HIMA, BYD, and
Huawei, embedding our auto service solutions into their online applications and panels, and providing various insurance products to EV
owners.
47
Our Business Model and Business Segments
The diagram below demonstrates the transaction process of our auto
eInsurance and auto services businesses, and the symbiotic relationship between them. We embed our auto service module, after customization
by our enterprise customers, into their own online loyalty applications. They then use the digital portal to procure the offline services
from our offline service networks. We also assist our insurance company partners to sell their insurance products through some of these
same auto service providers.
Our auto eInsurance
business
We generate revenue for our
auto eInsurance business by collecting commissions from insurance companies for the successful sale of their insurance products, which
are typically based on a percentage of the premium paid by insurance purchasers. Commission rates are typically set by insurance companies
and differ by product type, insurance company, and region where the products are sold. The commission rates are also subject to adjustments
by insurance companies based on their profit expectations, consumer demand, the availability and pricing of comparable products from other
insurance companies, and government regulation and policies. In particular, rates are impacted by price-setting regulations by the China
Banking and Insurance Regulatory Commission (CBIRC). Consequently, our average commission rates also vary by location and time of sale.
We offer auto eInsurance products
underwritten by major insurance companies in China. The auto eInsurance products we intermediate consist primarily of statutory automobile
liability insurance (“SALI”) and commercial auto eInsurance. SALI compulsory vehicle insurance for all automobiles in China
required by relevant laws and regulations, which covers casualty and property loss in accidents involving the insured vehicle. Additionally,
we intermediate various types of non-mandatory commercial insurance products for automobile owners, which cover damage caused to the insured
automobiles by collisions and other traffic accidents, falling or flying objects, fire, explosions, and natural disasters. We also intermediate
commercial third-party liability insurance products, which cover bodily injuries and property damage to third parties caused by accidents
involving insured vehicles, losses arising from vehicle theft and robbery and liability to passengers. We also facilitate the sale of
supplementary policies to cover additional losses such as broken glass and vehicle body scratches. From time to time upon enquiry of insurance
purchasers, we will also facilitate the sale of individual accident insurance and other property and casualty insurance products related
to vehicles or drivers.
We have digitalized our auto
eInsurance business using our proprietary technology to ensure efficient and friendly user experience. We employ artificial intelligence
(AI) technology to automate parts of the workflow, completing the entire insurance purchase process within a few minutes. We are digitally
connected to 35 major insurance company groups in over 1,250 insurance company branch offices (including the top 10 insurance company
groups with combined market share over 90%) in China through their systems, with a wide selection of auto insurance products. Our sales
partners have access to accurate traffic and vehicle data from car owners. These sales partners introduce and guide the car owners to
purchase insurance and then receive sales commissions from us.
By the end of 2025, we had
set up 31 branches across different cities. We have expanded our sales channels to over 64,000 sales partners. In China, insurance companies
typically establish local insurer branches in different provinces or cities to deliver their services and products. Usually, both insurance
companies and their branches have the decision-making ability to select their agency partners. However, when we engage with insurance
companies, the transaction is established digitally, and the business is allocated and executed by their branches.
48
Our auto services business
Through our digital platform,
we integrate the service capabilities of over 48,000 auto service providers to provide customized service solutions for our enterprise
customers. Our enterprise customers purchase these service solutions for their customers, who are typically members of their reward and
customer loyalty programs. Through a simple integration into their own loyalty platform, our enterprise customers can indicate their current
needs and budgets, which are then transmitted to our platform. These requests generate flexible and customized service solutions which
vary by type, price, scale, location, terms, and duration of services. Our dedicated operations team helps our auto service providers
reach clients in real-time, around-the-clock, and from all of our business locations.
Our auto service solutions include both high-frequency, routine services
and one-time, pre-booked services. The former includes car wash, oil change, car detailing, tire change, and other regular auto maintenance
services. The latter includes concierge chauffeur, flight pickup, driver service, road assistance, and car overhaul services. These services
are performed by the auto service providers connected to our digital platform; over 48,000 large and small businesses and individuals
in the auto service industry. As regulated by the PRC laws, the auto service providers are liable for tort claims for any damage resulting
from their services. Our enterprise customers are also liable for contractual claims by their end customers for any damage arising from
the services of the auto service providers.
Our auto services create value
for both our customers and the auto service providers. The auto market in China is highly fragmented, complex and localized, with non-standard
quality of service. End customer requirements are specific and dynamic. Based on our auto service providers’ feedback, without SunCar’s
marketing support, they often suffer from insufficient and unpredictable order flow. Our one-stop auto solution connects our customers
with a full-spectrum of services covering all 33 provinces in China, where we provide quality control, data security, and on-demand flexibility.
Based on past experience, our business scale and order volume have provided us with bargaining power versus the individual auto service
providers. This has enabled us to enforce our uniform standards of service quality, cost efficiency, and on-demand flexibility. Our smart
order distribution system automatically matches each instance of a client’s service need to the best auto service provider for the
job. After the job is completed, it records the client’s feedback for a sustained, accurate, and fair rating system.
We had over 1,520 clients
using our services in 2025, generating over 700 customized service solutions running on over 1,520 client applications for the year 2025.
We have developed a network of over 48,000 auto service providers in China by the end of 2025.
Our technology business
During our nearly two decades
of doing business in the auto service and insurance markets, we have acquired rich domain knowledge of our own business and our partners’
businesses. To fully digitalize our business, we have continuously worked to develop online tools and digital systems to empower our partners
to run their businesses more efficiently and seamlessly by connecting to our platforms. We have built modular online management tools
such as customer relationship management (CRM), order management, finance management, and visual analysis systems, based on our proprietary
hybrid cloud platform. All of our auto service providers and insurance sales partners use all or some of these online tools to manage
their daily work, allowing us the opportunity to monetize the online software we built.
We have been investing more R&D resources to accelerate the transition
of the existing online software modules into SaaS-based products. We launched our SaaS product with select customers in 2023, and are
scaling this offering on our proprietary hybrid cloud platform. We continue to migrate our current portfolio of online software products
to a 100% SaaS-based model. Prior to the SaaS-based product development which began in 2022, we had been selling our online software as
a technology development service, converting some of our service providers into our technology business clients. We expect to add more
features and make iterative updates to the product to enhance its capabilities and user experience. We currently market our technology
business first to our service providers and insurance sales partners. In 2024, we began expanding the technology service business to sell
to external clients, in addition to selling to our existing client pool.
49
Beginning in 2020, we started
to monetize our technical services by selling online software as a new source of revenue. For the year 2025, our technical services business
generated revenue of $54 million. Currently, this revenue comes from technology development service fees. We continue to develop our SaaS
(Software as a Service) model for recurring subscription revenue. In 2025, we continued to deepen our partnership with ZEEKR (NYSE: ZK),
having secured a contract in 2024 to develop and integrate our insurance platform into ZEEKR’s app ecosystem. We have also deepened
our innovative partnership with Xiaomi. With Xiaomi’s first vehicle delivery in April 2024, we have been co-developing a bespoke
insurance technology platform and expanding our embedded insurance sales for Xiaomi, including becoming Xiaomi’s partner for digital
insurance renewals. In 2025, we won the bid for the Huawei HarmonyOS Smart Car Alliance initiating a strategic partnership that extends
our embedded platform capabilities to Huawei’s smart car ecosystem. We expect to expand this business by developing more features
and by turning more of our after-service and insurance clients and partners into technology business clients.
Direct synergies between
our two major business segments
We believe that our strong capability in managing extensive networks
of auto service providers across China is a growth engine for our dual platforms of auto eInsurance and auto services. We believe it enables
us to realize synergies as we develop both of our business segments, as follows:
●
Cost-effective
end customer-acquisition for our auto eInsurance business by enabling our auto service providers to provide insurance sales referrals.
Auto service providers such as car wash and car detailing operators interact daily and closely with car owners, who, as insurance
purchasers, are the end customers of our insurance partners. Thus, we can leverage our extensive, established network of auto service
providers to acquire end customers for insurance partners in our auto eInsurance business.
●
Efficient promotion of our auto services by cross-selling to our insurance company clients. Insurance companies strive to promote their auto eInsurance products
and enhance the loyalty of their end customers by bundling their insurance products along with auto services. These auto services give
them a competitive advantage in a fiercely competitive market and with stringent regulations in their industry. We have established stable
and mutually beneficial collaborations with major Chinese insurance companies, which enables cross-selling and heightens the appeal of
both the auto services and the insurance products we facilitate on our platforms.
Our Value Propositions
We believe that our synergistic
multi-service platform provides unique value for enterprise customers and their end customers in the auto services and auto eInsurance
markets. We strive to promote the sustainable and healthy development of an integrated and digitalized service platform for car owners
in China.
Our value proposition
for our enterprise customers:
●
One-stop, plug-and-play,
round-the-clock service enablement. Our service solutions contain diverse service selections, provided 24 hours a day across
China. This empowers our customers with 24-hour, on-demand service capabilities to satisfy their end customers. The plug-and-play
customized service solutions are fully digitally operated and managed, via system-to-system integration between our customers and
us.
●
Simple, convenient, and cost-effective service. Management believes we have built and enabled an extensive network of high-quality auto service providers and established stringent service standards to ensure a consistent quality of service. Our digital platform allows our enterprise customers to purchase comprehensive integrated auto services from a single provider using a simple plug-and-play connection, thereby avoiding the costs of selecting, engaging, and supervising numerous scattered and independent service providers on their own.
●
Quality auto services
to end-consumers of our enterprise customers to increase their loyalty and satisfaction. We select quality auto service providers
and monitor them with regular training and supervision. Our management believes the quality of services provided by our auto service
providers enhances the loyalty and satisfaction of the end consumers of our enterprise customers.
50
Our value proposition
for auto service providers:
●
Cost-effective customer acquisition. Once connected, our digital platform directs the end consumers of our
enterprise customers (i.e. members of their loyalty and reward programs) to visit the stores of our auto service providers. This provides
our auto service providers with an additional flow of customers which is significant in both volume and consistency, all without them
incurring additional marketing expenses.
●
Online management tools for efficient operation. We provide our auto service providers with online management tools
to streamline their workflow and improve business efficiency. Although we have plans to monetize some of these online systems, we also
expect the basic functions and modules to remain free for auto service providers to use in order to ensure wide adoption of our digital
platforms.
●
Referral fees for our auto eInsurance business. Auto service providers on our platform can also act as referral service
providers for our auto eInsurance business. They refer to their end consumers (of the auto services) who are also our potential insurance
customers and then receive referral fees and other rewards when these referrals lead to successful insurance policy sales.
Our value proposition
for our insurance company partners:
●
Extensive network to
promote cost-effective auto insurance policy sales. We leverage our proprietary technology platforms and our extensive networks
of service providers to promote the sales of auto eInsurance products of our insurance company clients. This is facilitated by our
online platform, which connects our over 64,000 external sales partners to insurance products underwritten by our 35 insurance company
group clients (including the top 10 insurance company groups with over 90% market share), using our convenient online insurance
portal. Thus, we allow our insurance partners to leverage our extensive networks to promote their products with efficiency and scale.
●
Targeted sales
channels. Our sales partners consist of auto service providers and online car marketplaces with direct exposure to significant
car owner traffic. They connect their customers to the product offerings of our insurance partners, and we believe these
prospective customers are typically highly qualified prospects for our insurance company partners.
●
Efficiency with full
digital experience. Our online portal enables our insurance partners to complete the entire insurance underwriting process digitally.
With simple prompts from the insurance buyer, our system can realize automatic vehicle recognition, automatic quotation, online underwriting,
online payment, and insurance policy generation, saving time and cost for our insurance partners compared to traditional offline
policy selling.
Our value proposition
for our external insurance sales partners:
●
Referral fees. Our external insurance sales partners, which include a large number of our auto service providers, earn referral fees for successful referrals of insurance purchasers to purchase insurance products through our auto eInsurance platform.
●
Simple and convenient referral process. Our insurance portal integrates diverse products from 35 insurance
providers (including the top 10 insurance company groups with over 90% market share), which we believe provides marketwide selection
for insurance buyers. With basic training, our insurance sales partners can help the insurance buyer to finish the purchasing process
within a few minutes on their smartphones.
●
Enhanced consumer loyalty and satisfaction. For our channel partners such as Guazi.com, Souche.com, Chexiang.com, Cangoonline.com and, Qufenqi.com, we recommend and customize insurance products and provide assistance in claim and damage assessment to their consumers.
51
Our value proposition
for end consumers:
●
Convenient one-stop “supermarket-style” auto insurance shopping experience. End consumers can obtain accurate real-time information on various
auto eInsurance products and conveniently shop for policies while visiting the car wash, car detailing shop, maintenance facilities, or
car dealership.
●
Auto services for loyalty
points or at discounted prices. Our auto services platform enables end consumers to receive various quality services for free or
at discounted prices as a benefit for being members of the reward programs or customer loyalty programs of our enterprise customers.
We provide end consumers with the opportunity to conveniently redeem the reward points they accumulate for high-quality auto services.
●
Convenient and customized service experiences. The management believes the scale of our network of auto service providers
and efficient digital platform allows end consumers to conveniently choose auto services that best suit their particular needs at the
times and locations most convenient to them.
●
Complementary insurance claims assistance and related services. We, in collaboration with our insurance partners and external insurance
sales partners, provide comprehensive claims-related services to end consumers, including claims assistance and damage assessment assistance.
Our Auto eInsurance Business Process
The auto eInsurance policies
we intermediate generally have a term of one year. These policies are underwritten by insurance companies directly, and we are not a party
to the insurance policy or any other agreements with the purchasers of the policies.
Sales and Marketing
We market insurance products
to prospective end consumers sourced from a comprehensive and integrated omni-channel interactive marketing network connected by our digital
platform. These sales partners are comprised of external insurance sales partners such as referral service providers, external registered
sales representatives, and channel partners. All of our external sales representatives are registered with the CBIRC. We have embraced
the use of external insurance sales partners as a major part of our marketing strategy. This shift was prompted by the introduction of
the Insurance Law and the amended Provisions on the Supervision of Professional Insurance Agencies in 2015, which effectively eliminated
the requirement for salespersons to pass the qualification examination organized by the CBIRC and obtain a qualification certificate for
providing insurance referral services. In addition, the rise of the Internet and smartphones also prompted us to explore alternative marketing
methods. Consequently, we redefined our marketing strategies after 2015 to focus on external insurance sales partners connected through
our digital platform to our online insurance portal.

the services and products we intermediate, referring potential insurance policy purchasers to us and help facilitate our transaction process.

on their websites or billboards and notice boards on their business premises. They may also utilize our digital platform and online insurance
portal sites to provide information about the insurance products we facilitate to potential insurance purchasers, and then, refer the
prospective customers to us.

High level compatibility: An open architecture to support heterogeneous resource pools such as

C. Organizational Structure
SunCar conducts its operations
in China primarily through its PRC Operating Entities. ASGL was incorporated under the laws of the British Virgin Islands on September
19, 2012 and continued in the Cayman Islands in accordance with applicable laws. SunCar, including all of its subsidiaries, does not have
variable interest entity (“VIE”) structure. SunCar is a holding company and conduct substantially all of its business in China
through its subsidiaries in China (the “PRC Operating Entities”). It may rely on dividends to be paid by its PRC Operating
Entities to fund its cash and financing requirements, including the funds necessary to pay dividends and other cash distributions to shareholders,
to service any debt and to pay our operating expenses. Upon consummation of the Business Combination, ASGL and Goldenbridge became wholly
owned subsidiaries of SunCar.
Under PRC laws and regulations,
the PRC Operating Entities may pay dividends only out of their accumulated profits as determined in accordance with PRC accounting standards
and regulations. In addition, the PRC Operating Entities are required to set aside at least 10% of its after-tax profits each year, if
any, to fund a statutory reserve until such reserve reaches 50% of its registered capital. Each of such entity in China is also required
to further set aside a portion of its after-tax profits to fund the employee welfare fund, although the amount to be set aside, if any,
is determined at the discretion of its board of directors. Although the statutory reserves can be used, among other ways, to increase
the registered capital and eliminate future losses in excess of retained earnings of the respective companies, the reserve funds are not
distributable as cash dividends except in the event of liquidation. In addition, the Enterprise Income Tax Law, or EIT, and its implementation
rules provide that a withholding tax rate of up to 10% will be applicable to dividends payable by Chinese companies to non-PRC-resident
enterprises unless otherwise exempted or reduced according to treaties or arrangements between the PRC central government and governments
of other countries or regions where the non-PRC resident enterprises are incorporated.
